parts.description: The nerve passes under the inguinal ligament; its branching pattern below the ligament is fan type 40 %, sartorius type 37 %, posterior type 23.3 % (30 hips).
parts.citation: Giang DH et al. 2025 Medeni Med J 40(1):12-17 doi:10.4274/MMJ.galenos.2024.47042 PMID:40152087

parts.name: Suprascapular nerve under, suprascapular artery over, the superior transverse scapular ligament
parts.description: The suprascapular nerve passes through the notch under the ligament, branching proximal to the notch in 15 %, at it in 54 % and distal in 31 % (93 shoulders; notch depth 5.8 mm, width 7.8 mm); the suprascapular artery normally passes above the ligament (below in 3 % of 66 limbs).

passes.traversing_text: suprascapular nerve (under) and artery (over)
passes.through: superior transverse scapular ligament / suprascapular notch

parts.citation: Wang J et al. 2025 Surg Radiol Anat 47(1):181 doi:10.1007/s00276-025-03692-y PMID:40730883; Sethy S et al. 2025 Cureus 17(12):e99448 doi:10.7759/cureus.99448 PMID:41552191

parts.name: ECRB origin on the humerus (slightly medial and superior to the capitellum's lateral edge)
parts.description: The average site of origin of the extensor carpi radialis brevis lies slightly medial and superior to the outer edge of the capitellum; its undersurface rubs on the capitellar edge in extension while ECRL compresses it.
parts.citation: Bunata RE et al. 2007 J Bone Joint Surg Am 89(9):1955-1963 doi:10.2106/JBJS.F.00727 PMID:17768192

parts.name: Femoral attachment (medial epicondyle region)
parts.description: Band of retinacular tissue from the femoral medial epicondyle region to the medial patellar edge; ~55 mm long (Amis) / 5.3 cm long, 1.9 cm wide (Tuxoe, n=39).
parts.citation: Amis AA et al. 2003 Knee 10(3):215-220 doi:10.1016/s0968-0160(03)00006-1 PMID:12893142; Tuxoe JI et al. 2002 Knee Surg Sports Traumatol Arthrosc 10(3):138-140 doi:10.1007/s00167-001-0261-z PMID:12012030; LaPrade RF et al. 2007 J Bone Joint Surg Am 89(9):2000-2010 doi:10.2106/JBJS.F.01176 PMID:17768198

parts.name: Patellar attachment (medial patellar edge)
parts.description: Medial edge of the patella; its upper edge is easily identified medial to vastus medialis.
parts.citation: Amis AA et al. 2003 Knee 10(3):215-220 doi:10.1016/s0968-0160(03)00006-1 PMID:12893142; Tuxoe JI et al. 2002 Knee Surg Sports Traumatol Arthrosc 10(3):138-140 doi:10.1007/s00167-001-0261-z PMID:12012030

parts.name: Merging into the deep aspect of vastus medialis obliquus
parts.description: MPFL is overlaid to a variable extent by the distal VMO and its fibres merge into the deep aspect of the muscle.

parts.name: Medial patellomeniscal ligament (layer 3)
parts.description: Wide insertion at the anterior horn of the medial meniscus, narrow (0.3-0.5 cm) insertion at the inferomedial corner of the patella.
parts.citation: Tuxoe JI et al. 2002 Knee Surg Sports Traumatol Arthrosc 10(3):138-140 doi:10.1007/s00167-001-0261-z PMID:12012030

parts.name: Vastus medialis longus (VML)
parts.description: Partition with longer fibre bundles and larger PCSA; connected to the fascia lata by thin fascial bands; superficial and deep parts.
parts.citation: Castanov V et al. 2019 Clin Anat 32(4):515-523 doi:10.1002/ca.23344 PMID:30701597

parts.name: Vastus medialis obliquus (VMO)
parts.description: Partition with shorter fibre bundles and greater pennation; superficial part split into superior and inferior partitions; attaches to the adductor magnus tendon and medial patellar retinaculum. Waligora 2009 found no distinct VMO in 20 dissected limbs -> disputed.
parts.citation: Castanov V et al. 2019 Clin Anat 32(4):515-523 doi:10.1002/ca.23344 PMID:30701597; Waligora AC et al. 2009 Clin Orthop Relat Res 467(12):3297-3306 doi:10.1007/s11999-009-1052-y PMID:19690926

parts.name: Origin: tendon footprint on the pubis (anterior pubic ligament)
parts.description: Footprint 16.95 x 9.36 mm on the pubis; the adductor longus, adductor brevis and gracilis were in every cadaver attached to the anterior pubic ligament; neither adductor longus nor rectus abdominis attached to the inferior pubic ligament.
parts.citation: Capurro B et al. 2024 Arthrosc Sports Med Rehabil 6(5):100970 doi:10.1016/j.asmr.2024.100970 PMID:39534028; Mathieu T et al. 2024 Ann Anat 254:152238 doi:10.1016/j.aanat.2024.152238 PMID:38408529

parts.name: Conjoint tendons with adductor brevis and with gracilis
parts.description: Three conjoint tendons: adductor brevis + gracilis 90.9 %, adductor brevis + adductor longus 50 %, adductor longus + gracilis 50 % (22 cadavers).
parts.citation: Mathieu T et al. 2024 Ann Anat 254:152238 doi:10.1016/j.aanat.2024.152238 PMID:38408529

parts.name: Attachment to the inferior pubic ligament
parts.description: Adductor brevis attached to the inferior pubic ligament in 64 %, gracilis in 100 %; only these two attach there.
parts.citation: Mathieu T et al. 2024 Ann Anat 254:152238 doi:10.1016/j.aanat.2024.152238 PMID:38408529

parts.name: Oblique head
parts.description: Receives 1-3 branches of the deep ulnar branch (more than one in 95 %).

parts.name: Transverse head
parts.description: Receives 1-3 branches (more than one in 62 %).

parts.name: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve passes between the two heads
parts.description: The point where the deep branch of the ulnar nerve passes between the two heads is constant relative to the bi-styloid line, flexor carpi radialis and pisiform.

passes.through: between the oblique and transverse heads of adductor pollicis

parts.name: Superficial anterior oblique ligament
parts.description: Inserts on the trapezium. Bettinger 1999: sixteen ligaments stabilise the trapezium/TMC joint (14 on the trapezium, 2 on the metacarpal).
parts.citation: Bettinger PC et al. 1999 J Hand Surg Am 24(4):786-798 doi:10.1053/jhsu.1999.0786 PMID:10447171

parts.name: Deep anterior oblique (beak) ligament
parts.description: Substantial stabiliser; may pivot the first metacarpal in palmar abduction. Bettinger 1999: sixteen ligaments stabilise the trapezium/TMC joint (14 on the trapezium, 2 on the metacarpal).
parts.citation: Bettinger PC et al. 1999 J Hand Surg Am 24(4):786-798 doi:10.1053/jhsu.1999.0786 PMID:10447171

parts.name: Dorsoradial ligament
parts.description: Substantial stabiliser of the trapeziometacarpal joint. Bettinger 1999: sixteen ligaments stabilise the trapezium/TMC joint (14 on the trapezium, 2 on the metacarpal).
parts.citation: Bettinger PC et al. 1999 J Hand Surg Am 24(4):786-798 doi:10.1053/jhsu.1999.0786 PMID:10447171

parts.name: Posterior oblique ligament
parts.description: On the trapezium. Bettinger 1999: sixteen ligaments stabilise the trapezium/TMC joint (14 on the trapezium, 2 on the metacarpal).
parts.citation: Bettinger PC et al. 1999 J Hand Surg Am 24(4):786-798 doi:10.1053/jhsu.1999.0786 PMID:10447171

parts.name: Ulnar collateral ligament of the TMC joint
parts.description: On the trapezium. Bettinger 1999: sixteen ligaments stabilise the trapezium/TMC joint (14 on the trapezium, 2 on the metacarpal).
parts.citation: Bettinger PC et al. 1999 J Hand Surg Am 24(4):786-798 doi:10.1053/jhsu.1999.0786 PMID:10447171

parts.name: Proper intermetacarpal ligament
parts.description: One of two ligaments attaching independently on the thumb metacarpal. Bettinger 1999: sixteen ligaments stabilise the trapezium/TMC joint (14 on the trapezium, 2 on the metacarpal).
parts.citation: Bettinger PC et al. 1999 J Hand Surg Am 24(4):786-798 doi:10.1053/jhsu.1999.0786 PMID:10447171

parts.name: Dorsal intermetacarpal ligament
parts.description: The other independent metacarpal attachment. Bettinger 1999: sixteen ligaments stabilise the trapezium/TMC joint (14 on the trapezium, 2 on the metacarpal).
parts.citation: Bettinger PC et al. 1999 J Hand Surg Am 24(4):786-798 doi:10.1053/jhsu.1999.0786 PMID:10447171

parts.name: Lisfranc complex: dorsal ligaments
parts.description: Dorsal ligaments reinforce the capsules.

parts.name: Lisfranc complex: interosseous ligaments (strongest)
parts.description: The interosseous ligaments are the strongest; they vary considerably in course, number and insertions.

parts.name: Lisfranc complex: plantar ligaments
parts.description: Plantar ligaments reinforce the capsules.

parts.name: Lateral subtalar support: superficial, intermediate and deep layers
parts.description: Ligaments spanning the subtalar joint laterally and within the sinus/canalis tarsi are categorised into superficial, intermediate and deep layers; the inferior extensor retinaculum is a discrete, substantial structure.

parts.name: Anulus fibrosus laminae
parts.description: The anulus (excluding the transition zone) consists of 15-25 distinct layers depending on circumferential location, level and age; about half terminate or originate in any 20 deg sector.
parts.evidence: layer peeling + microscopy, L2-3 and L4-5, two age groups

parts.name: AM and PL bundle attachment centres (femur and tibia)
parts.description: Centres of the whole ACL and of the AM and PL bundle attachments were measured to arthroscopic landmarks (e.g. femoral AM centre 4.8 mm proximal to the bifurcate ridge and 7.1 mm posterior to the lateral intercondylar ridge; tibial AM centre 17.8 mm anterior to the retro-eminence ridge; PL: 5.2 mm distal to the bifurcate ridge, 8.4 mm anterior to the retro-eminence ridge on the tibia).

parts.name: Superior and anterosuperior sectors: variable labrum-glenoid relation
parts.description: A wide variety of morphologic labral-glenoid findings in the superior and anterosuperior sectors (36 cadaver shoulders), incl. the sublabral hole, which is a physiologic variant.

parts.name: Dorsal and inferior sectors: uniform, firm labrum-glenoid bond
parts.description: Relatively uniform anatomy with a firm bond between labrum and glenoid.

parts.name: Long-head attachment: four types (supraglenoid tubercle / labrum)
parts.description: Four types of biceps tendon attachment to the superior glenoid / labrum were identified (the abstract does not list them; Vangsness' scheme).
parts.note: Count of types only; the individual types are not named in the abstract and are not invented here.

parts.name: Antero-superior zone (clock-face quadrant)
parts.description: Free nerve endings and nerve end organs are more frequent in the antero-superior zone than in the other quadrants; healed-tear-like vascularity in four specimens.
parts.evidence: histology of 20 labra from arthroplasty patients
parts.citation: Alzaharani A et al. 2014 BMC Musculoskelet Disord 15:41 doi:10.1186/1471-2474-15-41 PMID:24529033

parts.name: Postero-superior zone (clock-face quadrant)
parts.description: As the antero-superior zone: more free nerve endings and nerve end organs than elsewhere.
parts.citation: Alzaharani A et al. 2014 BMC Musculoskelet Disord 15:41 doi:10.1186/1471-2474-15-41 PMID:24529033

parts.name: Disc proper (articular disc)
parts.description: Central fibrocartilage disc of the TFCC.
parts.citation: Winnett C et al. 2025 Australas J Ultrasound Med 28(3):e70012 doi:10.1002/ajum.70012 PMID:40606862

parts.name: Meniscus homologue
parts.description: Ulnocarpal meniscus homologue component, demonstrated sonographically.
parts.citation: Winnett C et al. 2025 Australas J Ultrasound Med 28(3):e70012 doi:10.1002/ajum.70012 PMID:40606862

parts.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris sub-sheath
parts.description: The ECU sub-sheath is counted as a component of the TFCC.
parts.citation: Winnett C et al. 2025 Australas J Ultrasound Med 28(3):e70012 doi:10.1002/ajum.70012 PMID:40606862

parts.name: Palmar-sided ulno-carpal ligaments
parts.description: Palmar ulno-carpal ligaments.
parts.citation: Winnett C et al. 2025 Australas J Ultrasound Med 28(3):e70012 doi:10.1002/ajum.70012 PMID:40606862

parts.name: Palmar distal radio-ulnar ligament
parts.description: With its foveal insertion, among the most important stabilisers of the TFCC (Mak 2017).
parts.citation: Winnett C et al. 2025 Australas J Ultrasound Med 28(3):e70012 doi:10.1002/ajum.70012 PMID:40606862; Chu-Kay Mak M et al. 2017 Hand Clin 33(4):625-637 doi:10.1016/j.hcl.2017.07.014 PMID:28991575

parts.name: Dorsal distal radio-ulnar ligament
parts.description: With its foveal insertion, among the most important stabilisers of the TFCC (Mak 2017).

parts.name: Anterior band
parts.description: Thicker part of the biconcave disc (anterior).
parts.note: Band thickness was measured in fetuses (Giambartolomei 2011); adult values are not given in the abstracts used.
parts.citation: Detamore MS et al. 2003 J Oral Maxillofac Surg 61(4):494-506 doi:10.1053/joms.2003.50096 PMID:12684970; Giambartolomei LA et al. 2011 Acta Odontol Latinoam 24(1):98-103 PMID:22010414

parts.name: Intermediate zone
parts.description: Thinnest part; collagen runs mainly anteroposteriorly, with a ring-like peripheral orientation.
parts.note: Band thickness was measured in fetuses (Giambartolomei 2011); adult values are not given in the abstracts used.
parts.citation: Detamore MS et al. 2003 J Oral Maxillofac Surg 61(4):494-506 doi:10.1053/joms.2003.50096 PMID:12684970; Giambartolomei LA et al. 2011 Acta Odontol Latinoam 24(1):98-103 PMID:22010414

parts.name: Posterior band
parts.description: Thicker part of the biconcave disc (posterior).
parts.note: Band thickness was measured in fetuses (Giambartolomei 2011); adult values are not given in the abstracts used.
parts.citation: Detamore MS et al. 2003 J Oral Maxillofac Surg 61(4):494-506 doi:10.1053/joms.2003.50096 PMID:12684970; Giambartolomei LA et al. 2011 Acta Odontol Latinoam 24(1):98-103 PMID:22010414

parts.name: Roof of the superior peroneal tunnel: superior peroneal retinaculum
parts.description: The tunnel is spacious; the superior peroneal retinaculum forms its roof.
parts.citation: Athavale SA et al. 2011 J Bone Joint Surg Am 93(6):564-571 doi:10.2106/JBJS.J.00662 PMID:21411707

parts.name: Floor, osseous component: retromalleolar groove of the fibula
parts.description: The retromalleolar groove has a constantly concave contour (60 dry fibulae) and forms only part of the floor.
parts.citation: Athavale SA et al. 2011 J Bone Joint Surg Am 93(6):564-571 doi:10.2106/JBJS.J.00662 PMID:21411707

parts.name: Floor, non-osseous component: lower part of the posterior intermuscular septum of the leg
parts.description: The non-osseous floor is the lower part of the posterior intermuscular septum.
parts.citation: Athavale SA et al. 2011 J Bone Joint Surg Am 93(6):564-571 doi:10.2106/JBJS.J.00662 PMID:21411707

parts.name: Contents beyond the two tendons: PB muscle fibres, peroneus quartus, split PB tendon, double PL tendon, accessory peroneal nerve
parts.description: Peroneus brevis muscle fibres were the most frequent additional content, then the peroneus quartus; split PB tendon, double PL tendon and an accessory peroneal nerve were observed.

passes.traversing_text: peroneus quartus, accessory nerve when present
passes.through: superior peroneal tunnel (under the superior peroneal retinaculum)

parts.citation: Athavale SA et al. 2011 J Bone Joint Surg Am 93(6):564-571 doi:10.2106/JBJS.J.00662 PMID:21411707; Wang XT et al. 2005 Radiographics 25(3):587-602 doi:10.1148/rg.253045123 PMID:15888611

parts.name: Peroneus quartus tendon inserting into the peroneus brevis tendon (variant)
parts.description: An accessory peroneus quartus muscle may insert into the PB tendon.
parts.citation: Wang XT et al. 2005 Radiographics 25(3):587-602 doi:10.1148/rg.253045123 PMID:15888611

parts.name: Bifurcated / mildly crescentic peroneus brevis tendon (variant)
parts.description: A bifurcated or mildly crescentic PB tendon is a normal variant to recognise on MR; a split PB tendon was also seen in the dissection series.
parts.citation: Wang XT et al. 2005 Radiographics 25(3):587-602 doi:10.1148/rg.253045123 PMID:15888611; Athavale SA et al. 2011 J Bone Joint Surg Am 93(6):564-571 doi:10.2106/JBJS.J.00662 PMID:21411707

parts.name: Lacunar ligament curved edge (medial boundary)
parts.description: The fascia lata turns back as the lacunar ligament, fusing with the pectineus fascia 1-1.5 cm below Cooper's ligament; its curved edge supports the transversalis fascia of the floor and bars the canal from entering the thigh.
parts.evidence: dissection of the posterior abdominal wall + pelvis (J Anat 1979)
parts.citation: Lytle WJ et al.  J Anat  PMID:468709

parts.name: Floor: transversalis fascia
parts.description: The transversalis fascia of the femoral canal floor turns down to form the medial wall of the venous compartment of the femoral sheath.
parts.citation: Lytle WJ et al.  J Anat  PMID:468709

parts.name: Venous compartment: medial wall from the transversalis fascia
parts.description: Medial wall of the venous compartment formed by the transversalis fascia of the femoral canal floor.
parts.citation: Lytle WJ et al.  J Anat  PMID:468709

parts.name: Medial (third) compartment = femoral canal (as taught; disputed by the source)
parts.description: The femoral canal is usually taught as the medial third compartment of the sheath; the author argues the lacunar ligament closes the canal off from the thigh.
parts.note: The abstract's own words: 'usually taught' vs the author's finding.  The other compartments of the sheath are not named in the abstract.
parts.citation: Lytle WJ et al.  J Anat  PMID:468709

parts.name: Radial aponeurosis
parts.description: First of the five components of the palmar fascial complex.
parts.note: Component list from Rayan 1999; 'what sub-structure belongs to which component' is an interpretation of the two abstracts and is not stated by either.
parts.citation: Rayan GM et al.  Hand Clin  PMID:10050244

parts.name: Ulnar aponeurosis
parts.description: Second component (ulnar side of the palm).
parts.note: Component list from Rayan 1999; 'what sub-structure belongs to which component' is an interpretation of the two abstracts and is not stated by either.
parts.citation: Rayan GM et al.  Hand Clin  PMID:10050244

parts.name: Central (palmar) aponeurosis
parts.description: The classical palmar aponeurosis; thickened longitudinal bands overlie the flexor tendons and are linked by the transverse palmar fascia.
parts.note: Component list from Rayan 1999; 'what sub-structure belongs to which component' is an interpretation of the two abstracts and is not stated by either.
parts.citation: Rayan GM et al.  Hand Clin  PMID:10050244; Watson HK et al. 1991 Hand Clin 7(4):661-668 PMID:1769988

parts.name: Palmo-digital fascia
parts.description: Transition between the palm and the fingers (the natatory ligaments belong here in the pathology literature).
parts.note: Component list from Rayan 1999; 'what sub-structure belongs to which component' is an interpretation of the two abstracts and is not stated by either.
parts.citation: Rayan GM et al.  Hand Clin  PMID:10050244; Watson HK et al. 1991 Hand Clin 7(4):661-668 PMID:1769988

parts.name: Digital fascia
parts.description: Fifth component; Grayson's ligaments and the bundles that pass deep to the neurovascular bundle at the flexor sheath of the middle phalanx are described in the Dupuytren literature.
parts.note: Component list from Rayan 1999; 'what sub-structure belongs to which component' is an interpretation of the two abstracts and is not stated by either.
parts.citation: Rayan GM et al.  Hand Clin  PMID:10050244; Watson HK et al. 1991 Hand Clin 7(4):661-668 PMID:1769988

parts.name: Palmar aponeurosis pulley: transverse fibres + vertical septa to the transverse metacarpal ligament
parts.description: Transverse fibres attached by vertical septa to the underlying transverse metacarpal ligament form a pulley over the flexor tendons; constant and substantial, overlying the synovial sheath.

parts.name: Vertical septa between the flexor tendons and the neurovascular tunnels
parts.description: Vertical septa fix the longitudinal bands to the deep fascia and the transverse metacarpal ligaments and pass deep between the tendon and the neurovascular tunnel.

passes.traversing_text: flexor tendons (central) and digital neurovascular bundles (either side)
passes.through: vertical septa of the palmar aponeurosis

parts.citation: Watson HK et al. 1991 Hand Clin 7(4):661-668 PMID:1769988

parts.name: Central band: bifurcation just distal to the PIP joint
parts.description: A central band continues into the finger, forks and dissipates just distal to the PIP joint; the two bundles pass deep to the neurovascular bundle and attach to the flexor sheath of the middle phalanx.
parts.note: Description of the pathologic (Dupuytren) cord; the normal counterpart is not distinguished in the abstract.
parts.citation: Watson HK et al. 1991 Hand Clin 7(4):661-668 PMID:1769988

parts.name: Zone 1: most proximal part (undivided ulnar nerve)
parts.description: In zone 1 the ulnar nerve is still a single structure with motor and sensory fascicles; compression here was found in 28 of 31 cases of ulnar tunnel syndrome.
parts.citation: Posner MA et al. 2000 Instr Course Lect 49:305-317 PMID:10829185; Murata K et al. 2003 J Hand Surg Am 28(4):647-651 doi:10.1016/s0363-5023(03)00147-3 PMID:12877855

parts.name: Zone 2 (distal; nerve divided into motor and sensory branches)
parts.description: Distal part where the nerve has divided; compression in 6 of 31 cases. Which of zones 2 / 3 carries the deep motor branch is not stated in the cited abstracts.
parts.citation: Posner MA et al. 2000 Instr Course Lect 49:305-317 PMID:10829185; Murata K et al. 2003 J Hand Surg Am 28(4):647-651 doi:10.1016/s0363-5023(03)00147-3 PMID:12877855

parts.name: Zone 3 (distal; nerve divided into motor and sensory branches)
parts.description: Distal part where the nerve has divided; compression in 19 of 31 cases; 17 cases (55 %) had compression in more than one zone.
parts.citation: Posner MA et al. 2000 Instr Course Lect 49:305-317 PMID:10829185; Murata K et al. 2003 J Hand Surg Am 28(4):647-651 doi:10.1016/s0363-5023(03)00147-3 PMID:12877855

parts.name: Aberrant hypothenar muscle crossing the canal (variant)
parts.description: Anomalous (accessory) abductor digiti minimi can compress the ulnar nerve within Guyon's canal.

passes.through: Guyon's canal with an accessory ADM

parts.name: Superficial part of the lacertus fibrosus
parts.description: Released first in the two-step release (R); after superficial and deep release the biceps lever arm drops 28 % in flexion and 50 % in supination.

parts.name: Deep part of the lacertus fibrosus
parts.description: Released second (R2).

parts.name: Median nerve beneath the lacertus fibrosus
parts.description: The lacertus fibrosus is a potential site of proximal median neuropathy; maximal perineural pressure at its level fell from 669 to 77 mmHg after release during elbow flexion.

passes.through: lacertus fibrosus (bicipital aponeurosis) at the elbow

parts.name: Superficial lamina of the posterior layer of the TLF (aponeuroses of latissimus dorsi and serratus posterior inferior)
parts.description: The superficial lamina of the posterior layer is dominated by the aponeuroses of the latissimus dorsi and the serratus posterior inferior.

parts.name: Attachment of the thoracolumbar composite
parts.description: The sacrotuberous ligament is one of the two firm attachments (with the PSIS) of the caudal thoracolumbar composite.
parts.note: Only this attachment is stated in the abstract; the ligament's own ischial / sacral attachments are not recorded by this reference.

parts.name: Anterior band (L5 transverse process to the anterior iliac tuberosity)
parts.description: Broad and flat; two varieties: type 1 from the anterior aspect of the inferolateral L5 transverse process, type 2 from its anterior, lateral and posterior aspects; fans out to the anterior iliac tuberosity.

parts.name: Posterior band (apex of the L5 transverse process to the iliac crest)
parts.description: Fusiform, from the apex of the L5 transverse process; widens like a small cone before inserting on the anterior margin and apex of the iliac crest; thinner than the anterior band with a smaller iliac base.

anchor.landmark: iliac crest, anterior margin / apex (MR) or upper iliac tuberosity (Hanson)

parts.note: Rucco places the posterior band on the iliac crest, Hanson on the upper part of the iliac tuberosity below the crest: a recorded disagreement on the iliac footprint.

parts.name: Short ligamentous bands from the L5 costal process to the iliac plate
parts.description: Present in 24 of 60 ligaments (about 40 %); a fibrous membrane connected to the ligament was found in 38 (63 %).
parts.citation: Dabrowski K et al. 2023 Surg Radiol Anat 45(2):169-173 doi:10.1007/s00276-022-03070-y PMID:36592184

parts.name: Type I: single band to the apex of the fibular head
parts.description: Most common form (72.3 %).

anchor.landmark: apex of the head of the fibula

parts.citation: Olewnik L et al. 2022 Clin Anat 35(3):375-382 doi:10.1002/ca.23842 PMID:35119143

parts.name: Type II: bifurcated (anterior slope + posterior surface of the fibular styloid)
parts.description: Dominant band to the anterior slope of the styloid process of the fibula, smaller band to its posterior surface.

anchor.landmark: styloid process, anterior slope and posterior surface

parts.citation: Olewnik L et al. 2022 Clin Anat 35(3):375-382 doi:10.1002/ca.23842 PMID:35119143

parts.name: Type III: double ligament (from popliteus tendon and from popliteus musculotendinous junction)
parts.description: Main band from the popliteus tendon to the anterior slope of the styloid process; second band from the musculotendinous junction of popliteus to the posterior surface of the styloid process.

anchor.landmark: styloid process, anterior slope and posterior surface

parts.citation: Olewnik L et al. 2022 Clin Anat 35(3):375-382 doi:10.1002/ca.23842 PMID:35119143

parts.name: Superior oblique band (SOB)
parts.description: Present in 15 of 19 elbows; 3.9 +/- 1.0 mm wide x 10.5 +/- 3.8 mm long; part of the deeper layer of the lateral elbow ligaments.
parts.citation: Barnes JW et al. 2018 J Shoulder Elbow Surg 27(1):e16-e19 doi:10.1016/j.jse.2017.07.031 PMID:28993111

parts.name: Inferior oblique band (IOB)
parts.description: Present in 13 of 19; 3.6 +/- 1.1 x 11.4 +/- 4.2 mm; inserts onto the anterior proximal ulna rather than the supinator crest.

anchor.landmark: anterior proximal ulna (medial to the supinator crest)

parts.citation: Barnes JW et al. 2018 J Shoulder Elbow Surg 27(1):e16-e19 doi:10.1016/j.jse.2017.07.031 PMID:28993111

parts.name: Anterior oblique band
parts.description: Present in 8 of 19; 3.8 +/- 1.7 mm wide.
parts.citation: Barnes JW et al. 2018 J Shoulder Elbow Surg 27(1):e16-e19 doi:10.1016/j.jse.2017.07.031 PMID:28993111

parts.name: Accessory lateral collateral ligament (localised thickening, supinator insertion)
parts.description: The described 'accessory LCL' is a localised thickening of the lateral complex arising from the supinator insertion independently of the IOB, attaching to the annular ligament and to the anterior proximal ulna at the bicipital fossa floor.

anchor.landmark: bicipital fossa floor, medial to the supinator crest

parts.citation: Barnes JW et al. 2018 J Shoulder Elbow Surg 27(1):e16-e19 doi:10.1016/j.jse.2017.07.031 PMID:28993111

parts.name: Adductor minimus (APm)
parts.description: Most proximal component; inserts on the lateral lip of the linea aspera (contrary to the classical medial lip).
parts.citation: Maguchi K et al. 2026 Clin Anat epub-ahead-of-print:n/a doi:10.1002/ca.70157 PMID:42237686

parts.name: Superior part of the adductor part (APs)
parts.description: Inserts on the lateral lip of the linea aspera.
parts.citation: Maguchi K et al. 2026 Clin Anat epub-ahead-of-print:n/a doi:10.1002/ca.70157 PMID:42237686

parts.name: Inferior part of the adductor part (APi)
parts.description: Only this component attaches to the medial lip of the linea aspera and the medial supracondylar line.

anchor.landmark: medial lip of the linea aspera and medial supracondylar line

parts.citation: Maguchi K et al. 2026 Clin Anat epub-ahead-of-print:n/a doi:10.1002/ca.70157 PMID:42237686

parts.name: Hamstring part (HP)
parts.description: Fourth component; innervated by the tibial portion of the sciatic nerve (= AM4 of Takizawa).
parts.citation: Maguchi K et al. 2026 Clin Anat epub-ahead-of-print:n/a doi:10.1002/ca.70157 PMID:42237686; Takizawa M et al. 2014 Clin Anat 27(5):778-782 doi:10.1002/ca.22274 PMID:23813615

parts.name: Perforator-defined segments AM1-AM4 (obturator vs sciatic territory)
parts.description: AM1 is supplied only by the obturator nerve; AM2, AM3 and AM4 by both the posterior obturator branch and the tibial portion of the sciatic nerve in 9.5 %, 95.2 % and 28.6 % of 21 limbs.
parts.note: Segments delimited by perforating arteries and the adductor hiatus; this row carries the segment definition, not a position.
parts.citation: Takizawa M et al. 2014 Clin Anat 27(5):778-782 doi:10.1002/ca.22274 PMID:23813615

parts.name: Origin tendons (superficial / deep membranous) and intramuscular tendinous arches
parts.description: Superficial and deep membranous origin tendons, insertion tendons and intramuscular tendinous arches were identified systematically with marked interindividual variation in position.
parts.note: Position of the tendinous arches varies between individuals; no zone is given in the abstract -> no geometry.
parts.citation: Maguchi K et al. 2026 Clin Anat epub-ahead-of-print:n/a doi:10.1002/ca.70157 PMID:42237686

parts.name: Origin: anterior part of the outer lip of the iliac crest
parts.description: TFL arises from the anterior part of the outer lip of the iliac crest.
parts.citation: Al-Hayani A et al. 2009 Folia Morphol (Warsz) 68(2):98-103 PMID:19449297

parts.name: Insertion: iliotibial tract slightly below and in front of the greater trochanter
parts.description: Attached to the iliotibial tract slightly below and in front of the greater trochanter; the ITB layers merge at the lower portion of the TFL.
parts.citation: Al-Hayani A et al. 2009 Folia Morphol (Warsz) 68(2):98-103 PMID:19449297; Huang BK et al. 2013 Radiographics 33(5):1437-1452 doi:10.1148/rg.335125171 PMID:24025934

parts.name: Gluteal aponeurotic fascia over the gluteus medius
parts.description: Posterior contribution to the fascia lata: the aponeurotic fascia covering the gluteus medius merges with the iliotibial band at the buttock and hip.
parts.citation: Huang BK et al. 2013 Radiographics 33(5):1437-1452 doi:10.1148/rg.335125171 PMID:24025934

parts.name: Adhesion to the iliotibial band (free outer surface)
parts.description: An adhesion connects the outer surface of the free part of the gluteus medius (not covered by the gluteus maximus or TFL) to the midportion of the iliotibial band.
parts.citation: Szymanski K et al. 2026 Ortop Traumatol Rehabil 28(2):99-112 doi:10.5604/01.3001.0055.8582 PMID:42545003

parts.name: Three layers of the proximal iliotibial band
parts.description: At the pelvis and hip the ITB consists of three layers that merge at the lower portion of the TFL; with the gluteal aponeurotic fascia it continues to the Gerdy tubercle.
parts.note: Layer names are not given in the abstract.
parts.citation: Huang BK et al. 2013 Radiographics 33(5):1437-1452 doi:10.1148/rg.335125171 PMID:24025934

parts.name: Distal tendon: aponeurotic membrane fused with the crural fascia
parts.description: The distal gracilis tendon has an aponeurotic membrane fused with the fascia cruris; a deep longitudinal fibrous bundle lies on this membrane.
parts.citation: Mochizuki T et al. 2004 Clin Anat 17(1):50-54 doi:10.1002/ca.10142 PMID:14695588

parts.name: Insertion: pes anserinus, medial to the tibial tuberosity
parts.description: With semitendinosus and sartorius the gracilis tendon inserts on the medial side of the tibial tuberosity; the first two attach superiorly and medially to the sartorius tendon.
parts.citation: Zielinska N et al. 2023 Folia Morphol (Warsz) 83(1):239-243 doi:10.5603/FM.a2023.0013 PMID:36811137

parts.name: Superficial longitudinal fibrous bundle on the sartorius
parts.description: A superficial longitudinal fibrous bundle lies on the superficial surface of the sartorius, fusing with the fascia cruris.
parts.citation: Mochizuki T et al. 2004 Clin Anat 17(1):50-54 doi:10.1002/ca.10142 PMID:14695588

parts.name: Insertion: pes anserinus, superficial layer (to the crural fascia in the variant)
parts.description: Normally the three tendons insert medial to the tibial tuberosity; in a rare arrangement the sartorius forms an additional superficial layer attached to the crural fascia well below the tuberosity.
parts.citation: Zielinska N et al. 2023 Folia Morphol (Warsz) 83(1):239-243 doi:10.5603/FM.a2023.0013 PMID:36811137

parts.name: Origin: anterior surface of the fibula and interosseous membrane (medial to EDL)
parts.description: Arises from the anterior fibular surface and the interosseous membrane medial to the origin of the extensor digitorum longus.
parts.citation: Zielinska N et al. 2021 Ann Anat 238:151762 doi:10.1016/j.aanat.2021.151762 PMID:33992748

parts.name: Insertion: dorsal base of the distal phalanx of the hallux
parts.description: Usually unipennate with insertion on the dorsum of the base of the distal phalanx of the hallux.
parts.citation: Zielinska N et al. 2021 Ann Anat 238:151762 doi:10.1016/j.aanat.2021.151762 PMID:33992748; Zdilla MJ et al. 2018 J Foot Ankle Surg 57(6):1218-1220 doi:10.1053/j.jfas.2018.03.031 PMID:30146339

parts.name: Accessory tendinous slips (to neighbouring bones, muscles, tendons)
parts.description: A vast majority of EHL muscles carry one or more accessory slips; the most common variation is an additional slip near the distal attachment; classification systems differ.
parts.note: Prevalence figures differ between the studies pooled by the reviews and are not reproduced.
parts.citation: Zielinska N et al. 2021 Ann Anat 238:151762 doi:10.1016/j.aanat.2021.151762 PMID:33992748; Zdilla MJ et al. 2018 J Foot Ankle Surg 57(6):1218-1220 doi:10.1053/j.jfas.2018.03.031 PMID:30146339

parts.name: Insertion footprint: base / tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal (mean 15 mm long)
parts.description: Footprint mean length 15 mm (10-specimen cadaver study cited in the abstract); its distal lateral extent is 15 mm from the tuberosity; the plantar fascia footprint lies alongside (PB and PF footprints extend into the Jones fracture site in 29 % and 43 % of 21 metatarsals).
parts.evidence: cadaver (10 specimens, as cited; 21 MT5 on CT)
parts.note: The 15 mm figure is reported in the abstract of Marcus 2026 (from the authors' earlier study); van Dijk 2020 provides the mapping; the earlier paper itself was not retrieved.
parts.citation: Marcus RE et al. 2026 Clin Orthop Relat Res 484(7):1331-1338 doi:10.1097/CORR.0000000000003827 PMID:41591313; van Dijk PA et al. 2020 Injury 51(12):2887-2892 doi:10.1016/j.injury.2020.09.020 PMID:32998823

parts.name: Right crus: L2-L4 vertebral bodies and the L2/3 intervertebral disc
parts.description: The right crus attaches to the L2-L4 vertebral bodies and the L2/3 disc; the thoracic duct overlies it at L3 and L2/3.

parts.name: Left crus: L1-L3 vertebrae
parts.description: The left crus inserts onto L1-L3; the cisterna chyli (70 % of specimens) overlaps it at the same levels.

parts.name: Sympathetic trunks emerge beneath the crura
parts.description: Both sympathetic trunks emerge underneath the crura at the L1/2 disc or L1 level.

passes.traversing_text: sympathetic trunk
passes.through: beneath the diaphragmatic crus (L1/2 disc or L1)

parts.name: Ventral root of the azygos / hemiazygos vein through the aortic hiatus or the crura
parts.description: Only the ventral root passes the diaphragm, variably through the aortic hiatus or through the crura; the dorsal root has no contact with the diaphragm.

passes.traversing_text: ventral root of the azygos (100 %) / hemiazygos vein (90 %)
passes.through: aortic hiatus or crura of the diaphragm

parts.name: Pattern 1: transversus abdominis and internal oblique aponeurosis fused into a tendinous layer
parts.description: Transversus abdominis muscle and the internal oblique aponeurosis fuse to form a tendinous layer. (30 cadavers; the abstract gives no prevalences).
parts.note: Patterns of the inguinal-canal posterior wall as reported by one series; prevalence per pattern not in the abstract; naming of the tendon layer as 'conjoint tendon' is not used by the abstract.

parts.name: Pattern 2: internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles form a muscular posterior wall
parts.description: Internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles form the muscular posterior wall. (30 cadavers; the abstract gives no prevalences).
parts.note: Patterns of the inguinal-canal posterior wall as reported by one series; prevalence per pattern not in the abstract; naming of the tendon layer as 'conjoint tendon' is not used by the abstract.

parts.name: Pattern 3: internal oblique muscle and its aponeurosis continue in the posterior wall
parts.description: Internal oblique muscle and its aponeurosis continue in the posterior wall. (30 cadavers; the abstract gives no prevalences).
parts.note: Patterns of the inguinal-canal posterior wall as reported by one series; prevalence per pattern not in the abstract; naming of the tendon layer as 'conjoint tendon' is not used by the abstract.

parts.name: Pattern 4: transversus abdominis muscle and its aponeurosis continue in the posterior wall
parts.description: Transversus abdominis muscle and transversus aponeurosis continue in the posterior wall. (30 cadavers; the abstract gives no prevalences).
parts.note: Patterns of the inguinal-canal posterior wall as reported by one series; prevalence per pattern not in the abstract; naming of the tendon layer as 'conjoint tendon' is not used by the abstract.

parts.name: Transversalis fascia: single thin layer, not part of the posterior wall
parts.description: A thin fascial tissue with only one layer of membrane, lying under the abdominal wall on the side of the peritoneal-cavity vessels; not involved in the composition of the posterior wall of the inguinal canal.

parts.name: Origin: internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles and their aponeuroses
parts.description: The tendon membrane of the cremaster is organised from the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles and their tendon membranes, extending on the spermatic cord and fixing it to the lower wall of the canal.

parts.name: Tissue plate of the deep perineal pouch (above the perineal membrane)
parts.description: A 4-5 mm thick plate between the ischiopubic rami, superior to the perineal membrane; about 80 % connective tissue; males about 10 % smooth + just over 10 % striated muscle; females about 20 % muscle cells, under 1 % striated.
parts.citation: Kampelmann M et al. 2025 J Anat 248(5):755-765 doi:10.1111/joa.70057 PMID:41123084

parts.name: Origin: perineal body, enveloping the bulbar urethra
parts.description: Paired striated muscle originating from the perineal body and enveloping the bulbar portion of the urethra; innervated by the deep branch of the pudendal nerve.
parts.note: Review of the male muscle; the female arrangement is not covered by this reference.
parts.citation: Lannes W et al. 2026 Int Braz J Urol 52(1):n/a doi:10.1590/S1677-5538.IBJU.2025.9917 PMID:41032754

parts.name: Insertion: medial surface of the coracoid process
parts.description: Tendon attached to the medial surface of the coracoid in 11 of 22 shoulders; those coracoids were longer and wider.
parts.citation: Umatani N et al. 2026 J Orthop Sci 31(4):783-788 doi:10.1016/j.jos.2026.01.008 PMID:41720692

parts.name: Insertion variant: superior or medial-to-superior surface of the coracoid
parts.description: In the other 11 of 22 shoulders the tendon attached to the superior or the medial-to-superior surface, extending toward the glenohumeral joint.
parts.citation: Umatani N et al. 2026 J Orthop Sci 31(4):783-788 doi:10.1016/j.jos.2026.01.008 PMID:41720692

parts.name: Origin variant: bifid belly / origin from ribs 4-6 (single case)
parts.description: Case report: right pectoralis minor bifid (medial and lateral fibres), left from the superolateral margins of ribs 4-6 to the anterosuperior coracoid; not a prevalence.
parts.note: Single case report of an atypical (inferior) origin; the usual origin pattern is not stated in the abstract and is not recorded here.

parts.name: Humeral insertion: tendon fully combined with teres major
parts.description: Latissimus and teres major tendons fully combined at the humerus.

anchor.landmark: intertubercular groove region (landmark wording not in the abstract)

parts.name: Humeral insertion: tendon partially combined with teres major
parts.description: Partially combined tendons.

parts.name: Humeral insertion: tendon fully separate from teres major
parts.description: Separate tendons; mean tendon width / length / thickness 48.4 / 56.2 / 6.2 mm (all 32 tendons).

parts.name: Accessory tendinous slips (to triceps tendon, brachial fascia, coracoid, anterior capsule)
parts.description: Slips connecting the latissimus tendon to the triceps tendon, adjacent brachial fascia, coracoid process and anterior joint capsule were found in nine specimens.

parts.name: Lumbar erector spinae, superficial (costal) part (= iliocostalis lumborum + upper longissimus thoracis)
parts.description: Arises by small fleshy slips from the posterior surface and the rostral / lateral margins of the erector spinae aponeurosis and inserts by slender flat tendons into the lower ten ribs.
parts.evidence: dissection of the lumbar erector spinae (J Anat 1986)
parts.note: Count of ribs and the attachments are Bustami's; the iliocostalis / longissimus equivalence is stated in the same abstract.
parts.citation: Bustami FM et al. 1986 J Anat 144:81-91 PMID:3693050

parts.name: Lumbar erector spinae, deep (vertebral) part (= lower longissimus thoracis)
parts.description: Arises by large fleshy laminae from the deep surface of the erector spinae aponeurosis and inserts mainly into the upper four lumbar and lower eight thoracic vertebrae.
parts.evidence: dissection of the lumbar erector spinae (J Anat 1986)
parts.citation: Bustami FM et al. 1986 J Anat 144:81-91 PMID:3693050

parts.name: Posterior (superficial) surface and margins: origin of the superficial / costal part
parts.description: Small fleshy slips of the superficial part arise from the posterior surface and the rostral and lateral margins of the aponeurosis.
parts.citation: Bustami FM et al. 1986 J Anat 144:81-91 PMID:3693050

parts.name: Deep surface: origin of the deep / vertebral part
parts.description: Large fleshy laminae of the deep part arise from the deep surface of the aponeurosis.
parts.citation: Bustami FM et al. 1986 J Anat 144:81-91 PMID:3693050

parts.name: Aponeurotic insertion: medial edge of the acromion (fibrocartilaginous)
parts.description: Longest aponeurosis (mean 28.9 mm); the only region with a fibrocartilage insertion, just posterior to the AC joint; contiguous with the deltoid origin.
parts.citation: Sugiura S et al. 2026 J Bone Joint Surg Am 108(6):450-456 doi:10.2106/JBJS.25.01007 PMID:41460933

parts.name: Aponeurotic insertion: posterior end of the acromioclavicular joint
parts.description: Aponeurosis 20.3 mm; thicker than at the clavicle; forms a contiguous complex with the superior AC capsule.
parts.citation: Sugiura S et al. 2026 J Bone Joint Surg Am 108(6):450-456 doi:10.2106/JBJS.25.01007 PMID:41460933

parts.name: Aponeurotic insertion: posterior edge of the lateral clavicle
parts.description: Shortest aponeurosis (mean 7.2 mm).

anchor.landmark: posterior edge of the lateral clavicle

parts.citation: Sugiura S et al. 2026 J Bone Joint Surg Am 108(6):450-456 doi:10.2106/JBJS.25.01007 PMID:41460933

parts.name: Variant: accessory slip from the distal third to the superior nuchal line
parts.description: Single unilateral case: slip from the distal third of the muscle passing above the superficial branch of the transverse cervical vessels to the superior nuchal line.
parts.citation: Gaydarski LL et al. 2023 Cureus 15(7):e42355 doi:10.7759/cureus.42355 PMID:37621798

parts.name: Anterolateral band (ALB)
parts.description: Commonly extends to the posterolateral acromion and may continue anterolaterally to end in a 'coracoacromial falx'; thicker at the acromion than at the coracoid; spurs form in it.
parts.citation: Fealy S et al. 2005 J Shoulder Elbow Surg 14(5):542-548 doi:10.1016/j.jse.2005.02.006 PMID:16194749

parts.name: Posteromedial band (PMB)
parts.description: Second band of the usual two-band ligament; thicker at the coracoid than at the acromion; may be mistaken for the entire ligament at arthroscopy.
parts.citation: Fealy S et al. 2005 J Shoulder Elbow Surg 14(5):542-548 doi:10.1016/j.jse.2005.02.006 PMID:16194749

parts.name: Additional bands (three or more)
parts.description: Multiple-banded ligaments (46 %) attach more medially at the acromion and coracoid; more than one band is associated with a rotator cuff tear.
parts.citation: Alraddadi A et al. 2017 Surg Radiol Anat 39(12):1323-1330 doi:10.1007/s00276-017-1900-5 PMID:28735412; Alraddadi A et al. 2021 Clin Anat 35(4):461-468 doi:10.1002/ca.23814 PMID:34851534

parts.name: Acromial attachment: medial aspect vs anterior edge
parts.description: Attached to the medial aspect of the acromion in 60 %, restricted to the anterior edge in 40 %.

parts.name: Coracoid attachment: medial end vs posterior aspect
parts.description: Attached to the medial end of the coracoid in 75 %, to the posterior aspect in 25 %.

anchor.landmark: coracoid process (medial end or posterior aspect)

parts.name: Capsule / ligament insertion on the acromion
parts.description: Capsular insertion begins on average 2.8 mm (2.3-3.3) from the medial acromion; mean capsular width 1.6-2.9 mm; the CA ligament insertion lies 3.5 mm from the medial acromion.
parts.citation: Stine IA et al. 2009 Arthroscopy 25(9):968-974 doi:10.1016/j.arthro.2009.04.072 PMID:19732634

parts.name: Capsule / ligament insertion on the lateral clavicle
parts.description: Capsular insertion begins on average 3.5 mm (2.9-3.9) from the distal clavicle; the trapezoid ligament begins 14.7 mm and the conoid 32.1 mm from the lateral clavicle.
parts.note: Measured on the anterior, posterior, superior and inferior edges (the abstract gives pooled means); separate superior / inferior ligament names are not defined in the abstract and are not used.
parts.citation: Stine IA et al. 2009 Arthroscopy 25(9):968-974 doi:10.1016/j.arthro.2009.04.072 PMID:19732634

parts.name: Posterior capsule (posterior sternoclavicular ligament)
parts.description: Review: the posterior capsule is the most important structure for sternoclavicular stability whichever the direction of injury; the costoclavicular, interclavicular and capsular ligaments stabilise the joint.
parts.note: Review article; the anterior capsule is not separately characterised in the abstract.
parts.citation: Morell DJ et al. 2016 World J Orthop 7(4):244-250 doi:10.5312/wjo.v7.i4.244 PMID:27114931

parts.name: Superficial layer / head (to the lateral epicondyle)
parts.description: In the two-layer pattern (29 %) the superficial layer extends to the lateral epicondyle; its proximal margin is the arcade of Frohse (membranous 68 %, tendinous 32 %).
parts.citation: Thomas SJ et al. 2000 J Hand Surg Am 25(5):936-941 doi:10.1053/jhsu.2000.16360 PMID:11040309

parts.name: Deep layer / head (to the ulna below the radial notch)
parts.description: In the two-layer pattern the deep layer extends to the ulna below the radial notch.
parts.citation: Thomas SJ et al. 2000 J Hand Surg Am 25(5):936-941 doi:10.1053/jhsu.2000.16360 PMID:11040309

parts.name: Posterior interosseous nerve through the supinator
parts.description: The radial nerve divides 3.6 cm proximal to the leading edge of the supinator; the posterior interosseous nerve passes beneath the arcade and leaves the muscle 3.8 +/- 0.9 cm distal to its proximal margin.
parts.citation: Thomas SJ et al. 2000 J Hand Surg Am 25(5):936-941 doi:10.1053/jhsu.2000.16360 PMID:11040309

parts.name: Origin: lateral epicondylar prominence (footprint 8.3 x 7.6 mm)
parts.description: Origin footprint 8.3 +/- 0.8 mm proximal-distal x 7.6 +/- 0.3 mm anterior-posterior, 0 mm from the joint capsule.
parts.note: Small footprint: far below the resolution of the body meshes -> text only.
parts.citation: Kacena-Merrell C et al. 2025 J Hand Surg Am 51(4):426.e1-426.e7 doi:10.1016/j.jhsa.2025.05.016 PMID:40622317

parts.name: Common extensor origin of EDC: footprint 5.1 x 7.3 mm
parts.description: EDC origin 5.1 +/- 0.6 x 7.3 +/- 0.9 mm; its distal-most edge touches the proximal edge of the lateral collateral ligament; LCL lies 10.3 +/- 1.5 mm from the epicondyle.
parts.citation: Kacena-Merrell C et al. 2025 J Hand Surg Am 51(4):426.e1-426.e7 doi:10.1016/j.jhsa.2025.05.016 PMID:40622317

parts.name: Humeral head (flexor-pronator origin)
parts.description: The humeral head shares a common aponeurosis with flexor digitorum superficialis of the ring finger; this septum within the flexor-pronator origin must be released from the proximal ulna to transpose the ulnar nerve.
parts.evidence: cadaver dissection + surgical series (J Hand Surg 1986)
parts.note: The abstract names the humeral head (and the ring-finger FDS septum); the ulnar head is not described in the abstract.

parts.name: Origin: proximal-radial quadrant of the transverse carpal ligament
parts.description: Origin area 105.8 +/- 30.3 mm2 = 18.4 +/- 4.8 % of the TCL volar surface (386.2 mm2).

parts.name: Superficial head (median nerve)
parts.description: Superficial head (sFPB) with its own median nerve branch arising 8.3 +/- 5.3 mm distal to the thenar branch (6 hands).
parts.citation: Rein S et al. 2025 Hand Surg Rehabil 44(2):102083 doi:10.1016/j.hansur.2025.102083 PMID:39805349; Loss J et al. 2020 Clin Anat 33(8):1176-1180 doi:10.1002/ca.23558 PMID:31894884

parts.name: Deep head (ulnar nerve territory)
parts.description: A deep head exists distinct from the superficial head; it is among the muscles reinnervated through the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
parts.note: Abstract: the transfer to the deep branch of the ulnar nerve shortens the reinnervation distance of 'the deep head of the FPB' (and 1st dorsal interosseous, adductor pollicis); its origin site is not given.
parts.citation: Rein S et al. 2025 Hand Surg Rehabil 44(2):102083 doi:10.1016/j.hansur.2025.102083 PMID:39805349

parts.name: Origin of the superficial head: distal aponeurosis outside the TCL (64.6 mm2)
parts.description: sFPB origin area 64.6 +/- 15.2 mm2, on the distal aponeurosis outside the transverse carpal ligament.

parts.name: Origin: around the ridge of the trapezium and the TCL (245.9 mm2)
parts.description: Largest thenar origin area (245.9 +/- 70.7 mm2; 17.3 +/- 9.6 % of the TCL surface), located around the ridge of the trapezium.

parts.name: Main belly (single in 58 %, double in 21 %, absent in 21 %)
parts.description: Appearance varies: one belly 58 %, two bellies 21 %, absent 21 %.
parts.evidence: dissection of both hands of 38 donors

parts.name: Accessory heads (flexor retinaculum, antebrachial fascia, long forearm flexors)
parts.description: Accessory heads with origin from the flexor retinaculum, the antebrachial fascia or the long flexor muscles of the forearm have been reported.

parts.name: Bellies: one to three (most variable hypothenar muscle)
parts.description: The abductor digiti minimi is the most variable hypothenar muscle, with one to three muscle bellies; supernumerary muscles associated with it in 2.5 % of 38 donors.

parts.name: Additional heads: flexor retinaculum, palmaris longus tendon, pronator quadratus tendon, antebrachial fascia
parts.description: Additional heads can arise from the flexor retinaculum, the palmaris longus tendon, the pronator quadratus tendon or the deep fascia of the palmar forearm (relevant to Guyon's canal).

parts.name: Additional head from the forearm aponeurosis (rare)
parts.description: Opponens digiti minimi is constantly present and mostly without variation; in few cases an additional head arises from the lower arm aponeurosis.

parts.name: Accessory head (Gantzer's muscle) from the coronoid process
parts.description: Disputed prevalence: 20.3 % of 473 limbs by MRI / US (all from the coronoid process, 79.1 % attached to FPL, 20.9 % to FDS in the US sample) vs 48 % pooled from 59 cadaveric studies (5903 limbs); the anterior interosseous nerve lies posterior to it.
parts.evidence: MRI / US n=473; meta-analysis of 59 cadaveric studies
parts.note: Prevalence disagreement recorded, not resolved: imaging series vs pooled cadaver series.
parts.citation: Torun BI et al. 2022 Surg Radiol Anat 44(9):1297-1303 doi:10.1007/s00276-022-03006-6 PMID:35974186; Asghar A et al. 2022 Anat Cell Biol 55(1):3-13 doi:10.5115/acb.21.141 PMID:34785621

parts.name: Accessory head to FDP (Gantzer's muscle variant)
parts.description: Accessory head of flexor digitorum profundus in 17 % (14 studies, 1627 limbs); the FPL accessory head is about three times more common.
parts.citation: Asghar A et al. 2022 Anat Cell Biol 55(1):3-13 doi:10.5115/acb.21.141 PMID:34785621

parts.name: Attachment to the lumbar transverse processes: lateral border (upper and lower corners)
parts.description: Quadratus lumborum attaches to the lateral border of each lumbar transverse process, at its upper and lower corners; transversus abdominis (via the middle layer of lumbar fascia) to the tip.

anchor.landmark: lateral border of the transverse process, upper and lower corners

parts.name: Psoas major: anteromedial surface of the lumbar transverse processes
parts.description: Psoas attaches to the anteromedial surface of each lumbar transverse process.

anchor.landmark: anteromedial surface of the transverse process

parts.name: Thickened attachment to the tips of the lumbar transverse processes
parts.description: The middle layer is thicker at the level of the transverse processes (0.62 mm) than between them (0.40 mm) and attaches to the tips; in 3 cadavers tension on it fractured a transverse process.
